title: Explaining KATAN-32 Third-Moment Leakage Non-Detection
summary: Testing found no sufficient evidence of third-moment leakage in the second-order KATAN-32 implementation; explaining this despite the missing combinational security guarantee remains open.

formal_statement.body: Explain the absence of detectable third-moment leakage in the evaluated second-order KATAN-32 TI despite the missing combinational security guarantee.

scope.domain: Empirical higher-order side-channel cryptanalysis of an FPGA KATAN-32 threshold implementation.
assumptions: The evaluation is performed on an FPGA with the PRNG enabled using a non-specific fixed-versus-random Welch t-test.
The combinational logic lacks a provable third-moment security guarantee.
parameters: Second order: DPA-resistance order of the evaluated threshold implementation
Third statistical moment: smallest moment lacking provable combinational security and target of the unexplained non-detection
300 million measurements: total test sample count, split evenly between fixed and random plaintext sets
Fifth statistical moment: comparison moment exhibiting systematic threshold crossings
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine why no third-moment leakage was detected under this evaluation despite the missing combinational security guarantee.

progress.summary: Using 300 million fixed-versus-random measurements, the paper reports no sufficient evidence of third-moment leakage, while fifth-moment threshold crossings suggest the measurement count should have exposed lower-order leakage if present. It notes several possible explanations but leaves their careful investigation beyond scope.
citation_labels: Begül Bilgin et al., Higher-Order Threshold Implementations
